leadText:
A Firebreather (Japanese: ひふきやろう Fire-breathing Guy) is a type of Pokémon Trainer that first debuted in the Generation II games. In Generation II, they were depicted as overweight clowns spewing out flames, while redesigned them and they now wear clothing designed after .

They specialize in Pokémon. They may, however, also use Pokémon that produce smoke, like and . In Pokémon Stadium 2, they specialize in Pokémon that know .

====Pokémon====
 

 

===Pokémon Gold & Silver: The Golden Boys===
A Firebreather by the name of (Japanese: タケオ Takeo) appeared in Let's Aim For The Goal. He signed up for a basketball tournament that both and Bugsy took part in. Bugsy pointed out to Gold that he was one of the strong opponents there and Bugsy himself would have been no match for him. During the tournament, Takeo managed to get to the final round where he faced off against Gold and Bugsy. Despite putting up a great fight, Gold ultimately defeats him.

====Pokémon====
 

 

==In the TCG==
 
 
Firebreather was introduced as a in the Pokémon Trading Card Game during the English Mega Evolution Series (the Japanese MEGA Series). It was first released in the Japanese expansion before debuting in the English expansion, with artwork by Naoki Saito. An version with artwork by the same illustrator was released in the same sets. This card allows the player to search their deck for up to 7 Basic (Fire) Energy cards and put them into their hand.
 

==Trivia==
Between Generations II and IV, one Firebreather got a name change from "Dick" to "Richard," likely due to the secondary meaning of the name Dick, itself a diminutive of the name Richard.
A sprite color change in occurs after Dick loses a battle against the player, from red to gray.
Firebreathers Dick and Ned are the only Trainers from Pokémon Gold and Silver to not appear in .
